source.title: A converse to a theorem of Gross, Zagier, and Kolyvagin
readSections: Read in full in the published version, the open-access PDF linked from the Annals article page for volume 191 (2020), issue 2, pages 329–354 (https://annals.math.princeton.edu/2020/191-2/p01), sha256 cfdfab6e62ac507be40d1f0bc8d9cb8371d95b42c5ae259fde054c70fb20c214, 26 pages, read 2026-09-23: §1 Introduction with Theorems A, A', B, C, D; §2 The proof of Theorem B (§2.1 Modular forms and abelian varieties, §2.2 Selmer groups, §2.3 More Galois cohomology, §2.4 The Heegner points P_K(f), §2.5 The Gross–Zagier theorem, §2.6 A p-adic L-function and a formal log of P_K(f), §2.7 Some Iwasawa theory for f and K, §2.8 An observation about hypothesis (irr_K), §2.9 Finishing the proof of Theorem B with Remark 2.9.1); §3 Theorem A follows from Theorem B; §4 A remark on the r = 0 case with Theorem E; and the references.

The arXiv preprint 1405.7294v1 (28 May 2014, 23 pages, sha256 of the PDF 9e4650618c83394c400a10e990759f9fba42113eedc79fe2fcbe029d6c8381ff; e-print archive sha256 80518dbef19f9dcf86686421f8c59c76af0bb1b2d6e69481b306d893162c0099, one file GZconverse-arxivready.tex of 1464 lines) was read alongside it for the exact LaTeX of every statement. It is the only arXiv version and predates publication by six years: the Annals page records Received 1 August 2013, Revised 1 December 2019, Accepted 2 December 2019, Published online 13 February 2020.

The two versions were compared statement by statement. The 19 numbered statements and their numbers agree exactly: Theorems A, A', B, C, D, E and Lemmas 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.3.1, 2.3.2, 2.8.1, Propositions 2.5.1, 2.6.1, 2.7.2, 2.7.3, Corollaries 2.5.2, 2.6.2, Conjecture 2.7.1, Remark 2.9.1. The one mathematical difference is in §§2.6–2.7 and is recorded as source issue E1: the published version places the anticyclotomic p-adic L-function in O^ur[[Γ]] and states Conjecture 2.7.1 and Proposition 2.7.2 as statements about ideals of Λ^ur ⊗_O L, where Λ = O[[Γ]] and Λ^ur = O^ur[[Γ]], whereas the preprint uses O[[Γ]] and Λ ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p throughout. The published bibliography is also updated (Wan's paper is Algebra Number Theory 14 (2020), the citation is to its Theorem 1.2 rather than to part (2) of Theorem 1.1 of the 2013 preprint; Bhargava–Skinner and Brooks are published). Every item below states the published form.
The Annals article page lists no erratum or corrigendum for this paper, and arXiv has no version after v1.

summary:
Skinner proves the first converse to the theorem of Gross, Zagier and Kolyvagin in analytic rank one for non-CM forms. Let f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) be a newform with trivial nebentypus and A_f the associated abelian variety, with M_f = End^0_Q(A_f). Theorem A says that if N is squarefree and either one odd prime ℓ has π_ℓ equal to the unramified quadratic twist of the special representation, or two odd primes have π_ℓ special, then rank_Z A_f(Q) = [M_f:Q] together with the finiteness of Ш(A_f) forces ord_{s=1}L(f,s) = 1; for a semistable elliptic curve (Theorem A') the hypothesis reads: non-split multiplicative reduction at one odd prime, or split multiplicative reduction at two. Theorem C replaces the arithmetic hypotheses by Sel_p(E) ≅ Z/pZ and a local condition at p, and Theorem E is the analogous rank-zero statement. All of these come from Theorem B, a p-adic criterion over an imaginary quadratic field K in which 2 and p split: under explicit ordinarity, irreducibility, ramification and discriminant hypotheses, if the Bloch–Kato Selmer group H^1_f(K,V) is one-dimensional and injects into the semilocal cohomology at p, then ord_{s=1}L(f,K,s) = 1 and A_f/K has rank [M_f:Q] with finite Ш.

The proof is p-adic and does not use a p-adic Gross–Zagier formula for a derivative or the non-degeneracy of p-adic heights. Hypothesis (e) and Nekovář's parity theorem give ε(f,K) = −1; the general Gross–Zagier formula of Yuan–Zhang–Zhang then reduces Theorem B to the non-vanishing of the Heegner point P_K(f) ∈ A_f(K) ⊗ M_f built from CM points on a modular or Shimura curve; the p-adic Gross–Zagier formula of Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna and Brooks, L^S_𝔭(f,1) ≐ (log_ω P_K(f))², reduces that to the non-vanishing of an anticyclotomic p-adic L-value; and the Iwasawa–Greenberg divisibility proved by Wan on U(3,1) gives L^S_𝔭(f,1) = 0 ⟹ H^1_𝔭(K,V) ≠ 0, whose contrapositive applies because hypothesis (e) makes H^1_𝔭(K,V) = 0 by a short Galois-cohomological argument (Lemmas 2.3.1 and 2.3.2) that is where the splitting of p in K is used.

The paper needs: the Eichler–Shimura abelian variety and the λ-adic representation V with local–global compatibility; Bloch–Kato Selmer groups, Tate global duality and the global Euler characteristic formula; CM points on X_0(N) and on Shimura curves with their descent to the Hilbert class field, and the ε_f-normalised Heegner point; the Yuan–Zhang–Zhang height formula; the BDP/Brooks anticyclotomic p-adic L-function, its membership in the Iwasawa algebra over the completed maximal unramified extension, and the p-adic Gross–Zagier formula at the trivial character; Greenberg's Panchishkin formalism and Wan's two-variable divisibility; Nekovář's parity theorem; Friedberg–Hoffstein non-vanishing; Ribet's irreducibility and level-lowering theorems and Serre's density theorem; and, for the alternative route at rank zero, Kato's Euler system.

items.name: The abelian variety A_f attached to a weight-two newform
items.statement: For a newform f ∈ S_2(Γ_0(N)) with trivial nebentypus, M_f ⊂ C is the field generated by the Hecke eigenvalues (the Fourier coefficients of the q-expansion at ∞), a totally real number field. The Eichler–Shimura construction attaches to f an abelian variety A_f over Q of dimension [M_f:Q], with End^0_Q(A_f) = M_f, characterised up to isogeny by L(A_f,s) = ∏_{σ: M_f ↪ C} L(f^σ,s), where f^σ is the newform whose q-expansion coefficients are the σ-images of those of f.
items.locator: §1, opening paragraphs, and §2.1, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: R14.5 plans the modular quotients J(X) → A_f with their endomorphism algebras, R29.5 the modular parametrisation and the L-function comparison, R19.1 the weight-two representation from the Jacobian with its coefficient field.

items.name: The theorem of Gross, Zagier and Kolyvagin
items.statement: Let r = 0 or 1. Then ord_{s=1}L(f,s) = r if and only if ord_{s=1}L(A_f,s) = [M_f:Q]·r, and ord_{s=1}L(f,s) = r implies rank_Z A_f(Q) = [M_f:Q]·r and #Ш(A_f) < ∞.
items.locator: §1, the displayed implication after the Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Gross–Zagier; Kolyvagin; Kolyvagin–Logachev)
items.note: BSD.3 and BSD.4 plan the analytic-rank-one and analytic-rank-zero implications for elliptic curves, HE.7 the integral classical descent and full Sha finiteness, GZ.8 the height identity. The A_f statement with its factor [M_f:Q] is the Kolyvagin–Logachev form and is the same theorem at the level of each conjugate f^σ.

items.name: The known converse in analytic rank zero
items.statement: For r = 0 the converse holds: it suffices that Ш(A_f)[p^∞] be finite for one sufficiently large prime p at which f is ordinary with respect to some λ | p. For a semistable elliptic curve it suffices to take p ≥ 11 of good ordinary reduction. This was established by Skinner–Urban for N not squarefull and by Wan for all N.
items.locator: §1, the paragraph following the Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin implication, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Skinner–Urban, Invent. Math. 195 (2014); Wan, thesis)
items.note: L1 plans the ordinary cyclotomic main conjecture in the Skinner–Urban form refined by Fouquet–Wan and L5 its arithmetic consequences; the rank-zero converse is the standard consequence of the Selmer-group side of that equality.

items.name: The rank-one converse for CM elliptic curves
items.statement: For r = 1 and A_f an elliptic curve with complex multiplication, the converse follows from Rubin's proof of the main conjecture for CM curves, Perrin-Riou's p-adic Gross–Zagier formula and Bertrand's non-degeneracy of the relevant p-adic height pairing; these are Theorems 8.1 and 8.2 of Rubin's paper. Since the theorems of the present paper assume N squarefree, A_f has no complex multiplication and the two sets of cases are disjoint.
items.locator: §1, the paragraph before Theorem A, and Remark 2.9.1(xii), Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Rubin, Invent. Math. 107 (1992), Theorems 8.1, 8.2, 9.5)

items.name: Theorem A: the p-converse for A_f of squarefree level
items.statement: Theorem A. Suppose N is squarefree. If there is at least one odd prime ℓ such that π_ℓ is the twist of the special representation by the unique unramified quadratic character, or at least two odd primes ℓ_1, ℓ_2 such that π_{ℓ_1} and π_{ℓ_2} are special, then rank_Z A_f(Q) = [M_f:Q] and #Ш(A_f) < ∞ imply ord_{s=1}L(f,s) = 1. Equivalently, in terms of Atkin–Lehner eigenvalues: either the eigenvalue of w_ℓ on f is +1 for some odd ℓ, or the eigenvalues of w_{ℓ_1} and w_{ℓ_2} are both −1 for two odd primes.
items.locator: Theorem A (§1), with the Atkin–Lehner reformulation in the paragraph following it, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Theorem A': the p-converse for semistable elliptic curves
items.statement: Theorem A'. Let E be a semistable elliptic curve over Q. If there is at least one odd prime at which E has non-split multiplicative reduction, or at least two odd primes at which E has split multiplicative reduction, then rank_Z E(Q) = 1 and #Ш(E) < ∞ imply ord_{s=1}L(E,s) = 1. Since the hypotheses force the root number of E to be −1, the reduction hypotheses exclude only the semistable curves of conductor 2ℓ with ℓ an odd prime having split reduction at both 2 and ℓ.
items.locator: Theorem A' (§1) with the paragraph following it, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Theorem B: the p-adic criterion over an imaginary quadratic field
items.statement: Theorem B. Suppose N is squarefree and p ≥ 5. Let K be an imaginary quadratic field with odd discriminant D. Suppose (a) p ∤ N and f is ordinary with respect to λ; (b) ρ̄_{f,λ} is irreducible and ramified at an odd prime that is either inert or ramified in K; (c) both 2 and p split in K; (d) if (D,N) ≠ 1 then for each ℓ | (D,N) the representation π_ℓ is the twist of the special representation by the unique unramified quadratic character, and each prime divisor of N/(D,N) splits in K; (e) dim_L H^1_f(K,V) = 1 and the restriction H^1_f(K,V) → ∏_{v|p}H^1_f(K_v,V) is an injection. Then ord_{s=1}L(f,K,s) = 1, rank_Z A_f(K) = [M_f:Q] = ord_{s=1}L(A_f/K,s), and Ш(A_f/K) is finite.
items.locator: Theorem B (§1), Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Theorem C: a mod-p Selmer criterion for semistable elliptic curves
items.statement: Theorem C. Let E be a semistable curve over Q such that there is at least one odd prime at which E has non-split multiplicative reduction or at least two odd primes at which E has split multiplicative reduction. Suppose there is a prime p ≥ 5 at which E has good ordinary reduction and such that (a) E[p] is an irreducible Gal(Q̄/Q)-representation; (b) Sel_p(E) ≅ Z/pZ; (c) the image of the restriction map Sel_p(E) → E(Q_p)/pE(Q_p) does not lie in the image of E(Q_p)[p]. Then ord_{s=1}L(E,s) = 1 = rank_Z E(Q) and #Ш(E) < ∞.
items.locator: Theorem C (§1), with its deduction sketched at the end of §3, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Theorem D: a positive proportion of elliptic curves of rank one
items.statement: Theorem D (Bhargava–Skinner). When ordered by height, a positive proportion of elliptic curves has both algebraic and analytic rank one. It is through variations of Theorem B, of the kind exemplified by Theorem C, that Theorem B plays a crucial role in the proof of this statement.
items.locator: Theorem D (§1), Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Bhargava–Skinner, J. Ramanujan Math. Soc. 29 (2014), 221–242)
items.note: ST.4 plans the Bhargava–Shankar orbit-counting Selmer theorems and their rank consequences and ST.5 the higher-moment and distribution refinements; the positive-proportion rank-one theorem is a consumer of those together with a p-converse of the kind proved here.

items.name: Theorem E: the analogous statement in analytic rank zero
items.statement: Theorem E. Suppose N is squarefree. If there is at least one odd prime ℓ such that π_ℓ is the twist of the special representation by the unique unramified quadratic character, or at least two odd primes ℓ_1, ℓ_2 such that π_{ℓ_1} and π_{ℓ_2} are special, then #A_f(Q) < ∞ and #Ш(A_f) < ∞ imply ord_{s=1}L(f,s) = 0. This gives an alternative proof of a special case of the rank-zero converse of Skinner–Urban and Wan.
items.locator: Theorem E (§4) with the proof sketch following it, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The strategy: from a non-vanishing p-adic L-value to a non-torsion Heegner point
items.statement: The proof of Theorem B runs: hypothesis (e) and the parity theorem give ε(f,K) = −1; the general Gross–Zagier formula then relates the Néron–Tate height of the Heegner point P_K(f) ∈ A_f(K) ⊗ M_f to L'(f,K,1), so it suffices to prove P_K(f) ≠ 0; the p-adic Gross–Zagier formula of Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna and Brooks gives L^S_𝔭(f,1) ≐ (log_ω P_K(f))², so it suffices to prove L^S_𝔭(f,1) ≠ 0; and the Iwasawa–Greenberg main-conjecture divisibility of Wan gives the implication L^S_𝔭(f,1) = 0 ⟹ H^1_𝔭(K,V) ≠ 0, whose contrapositive applies because hypothesis (e) forces H^1_𝔭(K,V) = 0. The method is essentially p-adic but, unlike Rubin's CM proof, uses neither a p-adic Gross–Zagier formula for a derivative nor the non-degeneracy of a p-adic height.
items.locator: §1, the discussion between Theorem D and the acknowledgements, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The λ-adic Galois representation V and its basic properties
items.statement: With T_pA_f the p-adic Tate module, V_pA_f = T_pA_f ⊗_{Z_p}Q_p, λ | p a prime of M_f, M_{f,p} = M_f ⊗ Q_p and L a finite extension of M_{f,λ}, set V = V_pA_f ⊗_{M_{f,p}}L. This is a two-dimensional L-space with a continuous L-linear G_Q-action ρ_{f,λ}, potentially semistable at p, unramified at ℓ ∤ Np, with V^∨ ≅ V(−1); for an embedding L ↪ C agreeing with M_f ↪ C one has L(V^∨,s) = L(f,s). The conventions for L-functions of potentially semistable representations are geometric: local Euler factors use characteristic polynomials of geometric Frobenius. The form f is ordinary with respect to λ if a_p(f) — the eigenvalue of T_p, or of U_p when p | N — is a unit in the ring of integers of L.
items.note: R19.1 constructs the weight-two representation with its coefficient field and lattices, R19.4 local–global compatibility away from p including the special case, R19.5 the potentially semistable and ordinary statements at p.

items.name: The K-twist of A_f and the factorisation of L(f,K,s)
items.statement: A_f^D is the twist of A_f by the cocycle in H^1(Q,Aut_Q A_f) given by the quadratic character χ_D of K, so that V_D = V_pA_f^D ⊗ L ≅ V ⊗ χ_D and L(A_f^D,s) = ∏_σ L(f^σ ⊗ χ_D,s); the natural map A_f × A_f^D → Res_{K/Q}A_f is a Q-isogeny whose kernel and cokernel are killed by 2. One sets L(f,K,s) = L(f,s)L(f ⊗ χ_D,s), whose sign of the functional equation is ε(f,K) = ε(f)ε(f ⊗ χ_D), and L(f,K,s) = L(BC_K(π),s−1/2) for the base change of π to GL_2(A_K).

items.name: The local root numbers of the base change and the sign ε(f,K)
items.statement: With ε_ℓ(π,K) = ∏_{𝔩|ℓ}ε(BC_{K_𝔩}(π_ℓ),1/2) one has ε(f,K) = ε(π,K) = −∏_ℓ ε_ℓ(π,K). If ℓ splits in K then ε_ℓ(π,K) = ε(π_ℓ,1/2)² = +1, so only primes inert or ramified in K contribute. If π_ℓ is the special representation σ_ℓ then ε_ℓ(π,K) = −1 when ℓ is inert or ramified, since there is a single prime 𝔩 above ℓ and BC_{K_𝔩}(σ_ℓ) is special. If π_ℓ = σ_ℓ ⊗ ξ_ℓ is the twist of the special representation by the unramified quadratic character, then ε_ℓ(π,K) = −1 when ℓ is inert (the base change is special) and +1 when ℓ is ramified (the base change is again a twist of the special representation by the unramified quadratic character). This uses that the root number of the special representation is −1 and that of its unramified quadratic twist is +1.
items.locator: §2.1, the final paragraph, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Kramer–Tunnell; Jacquet–Langlands, Propositions 3.5 and 3.6)
items.note: R16.3 plans local Langlands for GL₂ with the special representations and their ε-factors, R17.4 cyclic base change, AL.2 the local L- and ε-factors; the computation here is their combination for a quadratic base change.

items.name: Bloch–Kato Selmer groups of V and the vanishing away from p
items.statement: H^1_f(K,V) = ker{H^1(K,V) → ∏_𝔩 H^1(K_𝔩,V)/H^1_f(K_𝔩,V)}, where H^1_f(K_𝔩,V) = ker{H^1(K_𝔩,V) → H^1(K_𝔩,B_cris ⊗ V)} for 𝔩 | p and H^1_f(K_𝔩,V) = H^1(F_𝔩,V^{I_𝔩}) for 𝔩 ∤ p. By Tate's local Euler characteristic formula, local duality and V ≅ V^∨(1), dim H^1(K_𝔩,V) = 2 dim H^0(K_𝔩,V) for 𝔩 ∤ p, and local–global compatibility gives V^{G_{K_𝔩}} = 0, so H^1_f(K_𝔩,V) = H^1(K_𝔩,V) = 0. Hence for any finite S containing the primes dividing pN, H^1_f(K,V) = ker{H^1(G_{K,S},V) → ∏_{𝔩|p}H^1(K_𝔩,V)/H^1_f(K_𝔩,V)}.
items.locator: §2.2, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Bloch–Kato; Fontaine–Perrin-Riou; the vanishing cf. Nekovář–Plater, Lemma 3.1.3)
items.note: L2 plans the local conditions and the Selmer group as the kernel of the global-to-local map, L4 the finite Bloch–Kato condition once period rings are available, and L1 the local duality and Euler-characteristic input.

items.name: Decomposition of the Selmer group under Gal(K/Q)
items.statement: Restriction from G_Q to G_K induces an isomorphism H^1_f(Q,V) ⊕ H^1_f(Q,V_D) ≅ H^1_f(K,V), and the left-hand side is the decomposition of the right-hand side into the subspaces on which Gal(K/Q) acts trivially and non-trivially.
items.locator: §2.2, the display before Lemma 2.2.1, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Lemma 2.2.1: odd Selmer dimension forces sign −1
items.statement: Lemma 2.2.1. Suppose p ∤ ND and f is ordinary with respect to λ | p. If dim_L H^1_f(K,V) is odd, then ε(f,K) = −1. (Proof: the dimension is dim H^1_f(Q,V) + dim H^1_f(Q,V_D); one summand is odd and the other even, so by the parity theorem for Selmer groups of λ-ordinary modular forms one of ε(f) and ε(f ⊗ χ_D) is −1 and the other +1.)
items.locator: Lemma 2.2.1, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Nekovář's parity theorem for Selmer groups of ordinary modular forms
items.statement: For a newform f that is ordinary with respect to λ | p and a quadratic twist, the parity of dim_L H^1_f(Q,V) equals the parity prescribed by the sign ε(f) of the functional equation: (−1)^{dim H^1_f(Q,V)} = ε(f). This is Theorem 12.2.3 of Nekovář's Selmer complexes.
items.locator: Used in Lemma 2.2.1 and again in §3, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Nekovář, Selmer complexes, Astérisque 310 (2006), Theorem 12.2.3)

items.name: The p-power Selmer group of A_f and its relation to H^1_f(K,V)
items.statement: Sel_{p^∞}(A_f/K) = ker{H^1(K,A_f[p^∞]) → ∏_𝔩 H^1(K_𝔩,A_f(K̄_𝔩))}, Ш(A_f/K)[p^∞] defined likewise on H^1(K,A_f(Q̄))[p^∞], fitting in 0 → A_f(K) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p → Sel_{p^∞}(A_f/K) → Ш(A_f/K)[p^∞] → 0. With W = V_pA_f/T_pA_f = A_f[p^∞], Sel_{p^∞}(A_f/K) consists of the classes whose restrictions lie in the Kummer image H^1_f(K_𝔩,W), which by Bloch–Kato is the image of H^1_f(K_𝔩,V_pA_f); all three groups vanish for 𝔩 ∤ p. The maximal divisible subgroup of Sel_{p^∞}(A_f/K) is the image of H^1_f(K,V_pA_f), the injection A_f(K) ⊗ Q_p ↪ H^1_f(K,V_pA_f) has cokernel of dimension the corank of Ш(A_f/K)[p^∞], and H^1_f(K,V) = H^1_f(K,V_pA_f) ⊗_{M_{f,p}}L.
items.locator: §2.2, 'Connections with the Selmer group of A_f', Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: L2 plans the Selmer group of a lattice and its rational and divisible comparisons, L4 the Bloch–Kato/Kummer comparison; the statement here is their instance for an abelian variety with real multiplication.

items.name: Lemma 2.2.2: rank one and finite Sha give hypothesis (e)
items.statement: Lemma 2.2.2. If rank_Z A_f(K) = [M_f:Q] and #Ш(A_f/K)[p^∞] < ∞, then dim_L H^1_f(K,V) = 1 and the restriction map H^1_f(K,V) → H^1(K_𝔩,V) is an injection for each 𝔩 | p.
items.locator: Lemma 2.2.2, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The strict and the 𝔭-relaxed Selmer groups
items.statement: For S containing the primes dividing pN, H^i(K_p,V) = ∏_{𝔩|p}H^i(K_𝔩,V) and H^1_str(K,V) = ker{H^1(G_{K,S},V) → H^1(K_p,V)}, independent of S. When p = 𝔭𝔭̄ splits in K, H^1_𝔭(K,V) = ker{H^1(G_{K,S},V) → H^1(K_𝔭,V)} and H^1_{𝔭̄}(K,V) is defined likewise; both are independent of S.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.1: the semilocal image at p is two-dimensional
items.statement: Lemma 2.3.1. dim_L im{H^1(G_{K,S},V) → H^1(K_p,V)} = 2. (Proof: by Tate global duality H^1_str(K,V) is dual to H^2(G_{K,S},V), using H^1(K_𝔩,V) = 0 for 𝔩 ∤ p and H^2(K_𝔩,V) = 0 for all 𝔩; then the global Euler characteristic formula and H^0(G_{K,S},V) = 0 give the difference of dimensions 2.)
items.locator: Lemma 2.3.1, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Tate global duality and the global Euler characteristic formula
items.statement: For a finite set S of places of a number field K containing those above p and a p-adic representation V, the strict Selmer group is dual to H^2(G_{K,S},V), and dim H^0 − dim H^1 + dim H^2 is given by Tate's global Euler characteristic formula; together with local duality and the local Euler characteristic formula these are the inputs of Lemmas 2.2.1 and 2.3.1.
items.locator: Used in §§2.2–2.3, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: R02.4 plans Poitou–Tate duality and R02.3 global finiteness and the Euler characteristic; L1 their Selmer-theoretic application.

items.name: Lemma 2.3.2: injectivity at p kills the 𝔭-relaxed Selmer group
items.statement: Lemma 2.3.2. If dim_L im{H^1_f(K,V) → H^1_f(K_p,V)} = 1, then H^1_𝔭(K,V) = H^1_str(K,V) = H^1_{𝔭̄}(K,V). If in addition dim_L H^1_f(K,V) = 1, then all three vanish. (Proof: X, the image of H^1(G_{K,S},V) in H^1(K_p,V), is two-dimensional by Lemma 2.3.1; complex conjugation swaps the images X_𝔭 and X_{𝔭̄}; if X_𝔭 ≠ 0 then X = X_𝔭 ⊕ X_{𝔭̄} = X^+ ⊕ X^-, the one-dimensional c-stable X_f equals X^+ or X^-, whence X_𝔭 ⊂ H^1_f(K_{𝔭̄},V) and X_{𝔭̄} ⊂ H^1_f(K_𝔭,V), making X_f two-dimensional, a contradiction.)
items.locator: Lemma 2.3.2, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The two cases for the pair (f,K)
items.statement: Case I: every prime ℓ | N either splits or ramifies in K. Case II: N = N^-N^+ with N^- a non-trivial product of an even number of primes inert in K and N^+ a product of primes that split in K (so (D,N) = 1). Under (sqf), (sgn) and (ram) the pair (f,K) is in Case I or Case II.
items.locator: §2.4, the two displayed cases, and §2.5, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The Heegner point P_K(f) in Case I
items.statement: Let T be the Hecke algebra generated over Z by the T_ℓ, ℓ ∤ N, acting on S_2(Γ_0(N)), T_{M_f} = T ⊗ M_f, ε_f ∈ T_{M_f} the idempotent projecting to the f-eigenvalue system, 𝔭_f = ker ε_f|_T, X = X_0(N), ω_f the differential pulling back to 2πi f(τ)dτ, A_f = J(X)/𝔭_fJ(X) with quotient map φ, and ω ∈ Ω^1(A_f) ⊗ M_f the form with φ^*ω = ω_f. Let 𝔫 ⊂ O_K have norm N — possible because every ℓ | N splits or ramifies in K — so that C/O_K → C/𝔫^{-1} is a cyclic N-isogeny of CM elliptic curves and defines P ∈ X(H) over the Hilbert class field. With D_K = Σ_{σ ∈ Gal(H/K)}P^σ and D_{K,ℓ} = (T_ℓ − 1 − ℓ)·D_K ∈ Div^0(X), set Q_K(f) = (a_ℓ(f) − 1 − ℓ)^{-1}ε_f·[D_{K,ℓ}] ∈ J(X)(K) ⊗ M_f, independent of ℓ, and P_K(f) = φ(Q_K(f)) ∈ A_f(K) ⊗ M_f.
items.locator: §2.4, Case I, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: HE.0 plans ring class fields and reciprocity, HE.1 the CM points on X_0(N) and their descent to the ring class field together with the map to A_f through the modular quotient and the normalised Hodge class, CM.3 the Hilbert class field. The ε_f-normalisation over M_f is the only addition, recorded as the separate item heegner-normalisations.

items.name: Comparison of the normalisations of the Heegner divisor
items.statement: With D^0_K = D_K − #Gal(H/K)·∞ and Q^0_K = [D^0_K] ∈ J(X)(K), and with ξ the normalised degree-one Hodge divisor of Yuan–Zhang–Zhang, D^ξ_K = D_K − #Gal(H/K)·ξ and Q^ξ_K = [D^ξ_K] ∈ J(X)(K) ⊗ Q, one has ε_f·Q^0_K = Q_K(f) = ε_f·Q^ξ_K, because the cusps are Eisenstein (T_ℓ·∞ = (1+ℓ)·∞) and, by the expression for the Hodge divisor in terms of the canonical divisor, ξ is Eisenstein as well. The same comparison holds in Case II.
items.locator: §2.4, the paragraph on comparison with other constructions, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Yuan–Zhang–Zhang, §§1.2.2, 3.1.3)

items.name: The Heegner point P_K(f) in Case II
items.statement: In Case II, X is the Shimura curve over Q attached to the indefinite quaternion algebra B of discriminant N^- and an Eichler order O_{B,N^+} of level N^+ in a maximal order O_B, with an embedding K ↪ B such that K ∩ O_{B,N^+} = O_K. Replacing f by its Jacquet–Langlands transfer f_B, normalised as in Brooks §2.8 to be defined over M_f, and 𝔫 by an integral ideal 𝔫^+ of K of norm N^+, the constructions of Case I yield Q_K(f) = Q_K(f_B) ∈ J(X)(K) ⊗ M_f and P_K(f) = P_K(f_B) ∈ A_f(K) ⊗ M_f, and Q^ξ_K with ε_f·Q^ξ_K = Q_K(f).
items.locator: §2.4, Case II, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The hypotheses (sqf), (sgn) and (ram)
items.statement: (sqf): N is squarefree. (sgn): ε(f,K) = −1. (ram): if (D,N) ≠ 1 then π_ℓ ≅ σ_ℓ ⊗ ξ_ℓ for each ℓ | (D,N) and each ℓ | N/(D,N) splits in K. Since the central character of π is trivial, (sqf) implies that for each ℓ | N the local component π_ℓ is either the special representation σ_ℓ or its unramified quadratic twist σ_ℓ ⊗ ξ_ℓ; (sgn) implies that the number of ℓ | N with ε_ℓ(π,K) = −1 is even, so when (D,N) = 1 the number of prime divisors of N inert in K is even.
items.locator: §2.5, the displayed hypotheses, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Proposition 2.5.1: Gross–Zagier for the Heegner point of f
items.statement: Proposition 2.5.1 (Yuan–Zhang–Zhang). Suppose (sqf), (sgn) and (ram) hold. If P_K(f) ≠ 0 then ord_{s=1}L(f,K,s) = 1. The proof identifies P_K(f) = h_K·P(f_1)^ι with h_K = #Gal(H/K) and, for a symmetric ample line bundle 𝓛 with polarisation λ, computes ⟨P_K(f),P_K(f)⟩_𝓛 = ⟨P_K(f),λ(P_K(f))⟩_{NT} = h_K²ζ(2)L'(f,K,1)(f_1∘f_2^∨)^ι / (4L(χ_D,1)²L(Sym²f,2)vol(X)) by Yuan–Zhang–Zhang Theorem 3.13, so that P_K(f) ≠ 0 if and only if the height is non-zero.
items.locator: Proposition 2.5.1 with the computation following it, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Yuan–Zhang–Zhang, The Gross–Zagier Formula on Shimura Curves, Theorem 3.13 and §3.2.5)
items.note: GZ.8 plans the general Gross–Zagier pairing for factorisable test vectors in the quaternionic realisation, GZ.3 the rational automorphic realisations and the pairing of f_1 with f_2^∨, GZ.0 the normalisation conventions including the choice of line bundle and the zeta/eta factors.

items.name: Corollary 2.5.2: the order of vanishing of L(A_f/K,s)
items.statement: Corollary 2.5.2. If P_K(f) ≠ 0 then ord_{s=1}L(A_f/K,s) = [M_f:Q]. (If P_K(f) = ΣP ⊗ r_P with P running over a basis of A_f(K) ⊗ Q and r_P ∈ M_f, then P_K(f^σ) = ΣP ⊗ σ(r_P) for every σ : M_f ↪ R, so P_K(f) ≠ 0 if and only if P_K(f^σ) ≠ 0 for all σ; Proposition 2.5.1 applied to every conjugate then gives the corollary.)
items.locator: Corollary 2.5.2 with the paragraph preceding it, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The anticyclotomic tower and its Hodge–Tate characters
items.statement: K_∞/K is the anticyclotomic Z_p-extension, Γ = Gal(K_∞/K) ≅ Z_p with conjugation by c inverting Γ, and Ψ : G_K ↠ Γ the canonical projection; p = 𝔭𝔭̄ splits in K, λ is the prime of M_f determined by the fixed embedding Q̄ ↪ K̄_𝔭, and an embedding K̄_𝔭 ↪ C is fixed compatibly. A continuous ψ : Γ → Q_p^× is Hodge–Tate if it is so as a representation of G_{K_𝔭} or, equivalently by anticyclotomicity, of G_{K_{𝔭̄}}; the weights are then (−n,n) for an integer n, and ψ is the p-adic avatar of a unitary algebraic Hecke character ψ^alg of infinity type z^n z̄^{-n}, given by ψ^alg((x_v)) = x_𝔭^{-n}x_{𝔭̄}^{n}x_∞^{n}x̄_∞^{-n}·ψ∘rec_K((x_v)) with rec_K normalised so that uniformisers correspond to geometric Frobenius, whence L(ψ^alg,s) = L(ψ,s). Σ^c_𝔭 is the set of crystalline ψ of weight (−n,n) with n > 0 and n ≡ 0 mod p−1; crystallinity is equivalent to ψ^alg being unramified at 𝔭 and 𝔭̄.
items.note: L0 plans locally algebraic Hecke characters, their p-adic avatars through chosen embeddings, infinity types and the ray-class character space; L3 the Z_p-extension and its Iwasawa algebra; CM.4 the CM Hecke character/Galois dictionary.

items.name: The hypotheses (flt), (odd) and (L-lrg)
items.statement: (flt): p ∤ N. (odd): D is odd. (L-lrg): L contains a large enough finite extension of Q_p — it is enough that L contain the image of the Hilbert class field of K.
items.locator: §2.6, the displayed hypotheses, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The anticyclotomic p-adic L-function and its interpolation
items.statement: Assume (sqf), (sgn), (ram), (flt), (odd), (L-lrg), let S = {ℓ | pND}, O the ring of integers of L and O^ur that of the completion of the maximal unramified extension L^ur of L. There is an anticyclotomic p-adic L-function L^S_𝔭(f) ∈ O^ur[[Γ]] such that for ψ ∈ Σ^c_𝔭, ψ(L^S_𝔭(f)) = C(f,K)w(f,ψ)e_∞(f,ψ)e_p(f,ψ)Ω_p(ψ)·L^S(f,ψ^alg,1)/Ω(ψ^alg), where L^S(f,ψ^alg,s) = L^S(V^∨ ⊗ ψ,s) omits the Euler factors at the primes of K above S; Ω(ψ^alg) = (2πi)^{-2n-1}(2π)^{1-2n}Ω^{4n}D^{n-1/2} with Ω a period of an elliptic curve E_0 with CM by O_K; Ω_p(ψ) = Ω_p^{4n}; e_∞(f,ψ) = 4(2π)^{-2n-1}Γ(n)Γ(n+1); e_p(f,ψ) = (1 − a_p(f)ψ^alg(𝔭̄)p^{-1} + ψ^alg(𝔭̄)²p^{-1})/(1 − a_p(f)ψ^alg(𝔭)p^{-1} + ψ^alg(𝔭)²p^{-1}); w(f,ψ) = ψ(W) for a unit W ∈ O^ur[[Γ]]^× with w(f,1) = w_K; and C(f,K) a non-zero constant depending on f and K. One writes L^S_𝔭(f,ψ) = ψ(L^S_𝔭(f)).
items.locator: §2.6, the displayed interpolation formula, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna; Brooks; Brakočević; Eischen–Harris–Li–Skinner; Wan)
items.note: GZ.9 plans the construction of the BDP/Brooks p-adic L-function in the weight-two Heegner setting at a prime split in the imaginary quadratic field, with its actual interpolation range, CM periods and removed Euler factors, in both the modular-curve and the quaternionic case.

items.name: The p-adic L-function belongs to the Iwasawa algebra
items.statement: The functions constructed in Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna and in Brooks are a priori only continuous on Γ. That L^S_𝔭(f) belongs to the Iwasawa algebra O^ur[[Γ]] requires an additional argument, essentially the extension of the interpolation formulas to characters ramified at the primes above p, as carried out by Brakočević; it also follows from the constructions of Eischen–Harris–Li–Skinner and of Wan, and, when some ℓ | N is inert or ramified in K, the function is constructed directly in those two references. It can be related to a specialisation of Hida's three-variable Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-function.
items.locator: §2.6, the paragraph after the interpolation formula, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Brakočević, IMRN 2011; Eischen–Harris–Li–Skinner; Wan, Algebra Number Theory 14 (2020); Hida, Ann. Inst. Fourier 38 (1988))

items.name: Identification with the BDP and Brooks p-adic L-functions
items.statement: For ψ ∈ Σ^c_𝔭 let χ be the Hecke character with χ^{-1} = ψ^alg|Nm(·)|_Q. Then L^S_𝔭(f) is the imprimitive variant — the Euler factors at the primes of S not dividing p removed — of the p-adic L-function denoted L_p(f,χ) in Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna (Case I) and in Brooks (Case II); the corresponding set of χ is Σ^{(2)}_{cc}(𝔫), respectively Σ^{(2)}_{cc}(𝔫^+), and the interpolated values are given there in terms of L(f,χ^{-1},0) = L(f,ψ^alg,1). In that notation e_∞(f,ψ)w_K(2πi)^{1+2n} = C(f,χ,1), w(f,ψ) = w_K w(f,χ)^{-1}, and C(f,K) is the constant α(f,f_{GL_2})^{-1} of Brooks.
items.locator: §2.6, the paragraph beginning 'For ψ ∈ Σ^c_𝔭', Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Proposition 2.6.1: the p-adic Gross–Zagier formula at the BDP point
items.statement: Proposition 2.6.1 (Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna; Brooks). Suppose (sqf), (sgn), (ram), (flt) and (odd) hold. Then L^S_𝔭(f,1) ≐ (log_ω P_K(f))², where ≐ is equality up to a non-zero constant depending also on the eigenvalues at the primes in S, ω ∈ Ω^1(A_f) ⊗ M_f satisfies φ^*ω = ω_f, and log_ω : A_f(K_𝔭) ⊗ L → K̄_𝔭 is the formal logarithm determined by ω. The trivial character ψ = 1, the BDP point, is not in Σ^c_𝔭.
items.locator: Proposition 2.6.1, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna, Pacific J. Math. 260 (2012), Theorem 3.12; Brooks, IMRN 2015, Proposition 8.13)
items.note: GZ.9 plans the p-adic Waldspurger identity at the weight-two point outside the interpolation range — the specified specialisation equals the square of the formal logarithm of the corresponding Heegner point times explicit local factors — including the quaternionic variant of Brooks Proposition 8.13.

items.name: Reduction of Proposition 2.6.1 to the published formulas
items.statement: In Case I, Proposition 2.6.1 is Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna Theorem 3.12, whose formula has log_ω P_f with P_f = φ(Q^0_K); since log_ω P_K = log_{ω_f}Q^0_K and ε_f·ω_f = ω_f, one has log_{ω_f}Q^0_K = log_{ω_f}ε_f·Q^0_K = log_{ω_f}Q_K(f) = log_ω P_K(f), which gives the stated form. In Case II the proposition follows in the same way from Brooks Proposition 8.13.
items.locator: §2.6, the paragraph after Proposition 2.6.1, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Corollary 2.6.2: non-vanishing of the Heegner point is non-vanishing of the p-adic L-value
items.statement: Corollary 2.6.2. P_K(f) ≠ 0 if and only if L^S_𝔭(f,1) ≠ 0.
items.locator: Corollary 2.6.2, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The big Galois module M and the Iwasawa–Greenberg Selmer group
items.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of L, T ⊂ V a G_Q-stable O-lattice, Λ = O[[Γ]] and Λ^ur = O^ur[[Γ]] with O^ur the ring of integers of the completion of the maximal unramified extension of L. Viewing Ψ : G_K ↠ Γ as a continuous Λ^×-valued character and Λ^* = Hom_cts(Λ,Q_p/Z_p), set M = T ⊗_O Λ^*(Ψ^{-1}), the discrete Λ-module T ⊗_O Λ^* with G_K acting by ρ_{f,λ} ⊗ Ψ^{-1}. With S = {ℓ | pND}, Sel_∞(f,K,S) = ker{H^1(G_{K,S},M) → H^1(I_𝔭,M)}, its Pontryagin dual X_∞(f,K,S) = Hom_Λ(Sel_∞(f,K,S),Λ^*) is a finitely generated Λ-module, and Ch_Λ(f,K,S) is its characteristic ideal, non-zero exactly when X_∞(f,K,S) is Λ-torsion.

items.name: Characteristic ideals of finitely generated Iwasawa modules
items.statement: For a finitely generated module over the Iwasawa algebra of a one-dimensional p-adic Lie group, the characteristic ideal is defined and principal, is non-zero exactly when the module is torsion, and an inclusion char ⊆ (γ−1) forces the (γ−1)-coinvariants to be infinite. These are the structure-theoretic facts used to pass from the divisibility of Proposition 2.7.2 to the statement about Selmer groups.
items.locator: Used in §2.7, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354
items.note: L4 plans the Weierstrass theory and the module structure over the Iwasawa algebra with characteristic ideals, L5 determinants, specialisation and exactness.

items.name: Sel_∞ as a Greenberg Selmer group and the Panchishkin condition
items.statement: For ψ ∈ Σ^c_𝔭 of weight (−n,n) with n > 0, the induced representation Ind_{G_K}^{G_Q}(V ⊗ ψ^{-1}) satisfies Greenberg's Panchishkin condition: its restriction to G_{Q_p} is (V ⊗ ψ^{-1}) ⊕ (V ⊗ ψ^{-c}), the first summand being (V ⊗ ψ^{-1})|_{G_{K_𝔭}} with non-negative Hodge–Tate weights n and n−1 and the second (V ⊗ ψ^{-1})|_{G_{K_{𝔭̄}}} with negative weights −n and −n−1, and the subspace with negative weights has dimension equal to that of the +1-eigenspace of complex conjugation. Moreover M[γ−ψ(γ)] ≅ (T ⊗ ψ^{-1}) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p for a topological generator γ, so M is the discrete module of the deformation T ⊗ Λ(Ψ^{-1}) of T, which has a Zariski-dense set of Panchishkin specialisations, and Sel_∞(f,K,S) is the corresponding imprimitive Greenberg Selmer group. The conventions for Hodge–Tate weights are the negative of Greenberg's.
items.locator: §2.7, the paragraph following the definition of Ch_Λ, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Greenberg, Iwasawa theory and p-adic deformations of motives, §§3–4)
items.note: L0 plans the three formulations of the main conjecture, including the Greenberg/ordinary Selmer formulation with its Panchishkin subspace; L2 the Greenberg local conditions themselves. What is specific here is the G_K-version for the anticyclotomic deformation, recorded separately in the item iwasawa-modules.

items.name: The hypotheses (irr) and (irr_K)
items.statement: (irr): ρ̄_{f,λ} is an irreducible G_Q-representation. (irr_K): ρ̄_{f,λ}|_{G_K} is irreducible.

items.name: Conjecture 2.7.1: the Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjecture for M
items.statement: Conjecture 2.7.1. Assuming (irr_K), Ch_Λ(f,K,S) and L^S_𝔭(f) generate the same ideal of Λ^ur ⊗_O L. This is essentially the Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjecture for M, the choice of p-adic L-function being dictated by the expectation that the order of the Selmer group for V ⊗ ψ^{-1} is related to the L-value L(V^∨ ⊗ ψ,1).
items.locator: Conjecture 2.7.1 with its footnote, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The hypotheses (big), (ord), (spl) and (res)
items.statement: (big): p ≥ 5. (ord): f is ordinary with respect to λ. (spl): both 2 and p split in K. (res): ρ̄_{f,λ} is ramified at some odd prime ℓ | N that is inert or ramified in K.
items.locator: §2.7, the displayed hypotheses before Proposition 2.7.2, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Wan's Iwasawa main conjecture for Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-functions
items.statement: Wan's theorem, proved by the Eisenstein-congruence method on the unitary group U(3,1) following Skinner–Urban, gives the divisibility of characteristic ideals by the two-variable Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-function 𝓛^{Σ,Hida}_{f_0,K,ξ} ∈ O^ur[[Γ_K]] over the Galois group Γ_K ≅ Z_p² of the composite of all Z_p-extensions of K: for Σ the relevant finite set, the ideal of O^ur[[Γ_K]] ⊗_O L generated by char_{O[[Γ_K]]}X^Σ_{f_0,K,ξ} is contained in the ideal generated by 𝓛^{Σ,Hida}_{f_0,K,ξ}. Its hypotheses include p ≥ 5, ordinarity, the splitting of 2 and p in K, irreducibility of the residual representation and its ramification at an odd prime of N that is inert or ramified in K.
items.locator: Used through Proposition 2.7.2, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Wan, Iwasawa main conjecture for Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-functions, Algebra Number Theory 14 (2020), 383–483, Theorem 1.2)
items.note: L2 plans exactly the U(3,1) Eisenstein/Rankin–Selberg families with the auxiliary imaginary quadratic field, its two-variable extension and the two-variable divisibility, including the exceptional height-one primes.

items.name: Proposition 2.7.2 and its deduction from Wan's theorem
items.statement: Proposition 2.7.2. Under (sqf), (flt), (L-lrg), (irr_K), (sgn), (odd), (big), (ord), (spl) and (res), the ideal of Λ^ur ⊗_O L generated by Ch_Λ(f,K,S) is contained in the ideal generated by L^S_𝔭(f). The deduction: fix ψ_0 ∈ Σ^c_𝔭 of weight (−n_0,n_0) with n_0 > 6, let ψ^alg_0 be the associated algebraic Hecke character and ξ = ψ^alg_0 ω with ω the Teichmüller Hecke character; then π, the ordinary stabilisation f_0 of f, and ξ satisfy the hypotheses of Wan's theorem. Under the composition O^ur[[Γ_K]] → Λ^ur, γ ↦ ψ_0(γ)^{-1}γ, the function 𝓛^{Σ,Hida}_{f_0,K,ξ} maps to L^S_𝔭(f), and under the same base change Sel^Σ_{f_0,K,ξ} becomes Sel_∞(f,K,S) and X^Σ_{f_0,K,ξ} becomes X_∞(f,K,S); the inclusion of ideals then follows because the rings involved are unique factorisation domains and the characteristic ideals are principal.
items.locator: Proposition 2.7.2 with the two paragraphs explaining its deduction, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The control diagram and the consequence of a vanishing p-adic L-value
items.statement: Let W = M[γ−1] = T ⊗ Q_p/Z_p, Sel_𝔭(f,K,S) = ker{H^1(G_{K,S},W) → H^1(I_𝔭,W)} and X_𝔭(f,K,S) its Pontryagin dual. Assuming (irr_K), H^1(G_{K,S},W) = H^1(G_{K,S},M)[γ−1], and the exactness of the bottom row of the commutative diagram built from 0 → W → M →^{γ−1} M → 0 shows that Sel_𝔭(f,K,S) is contained in Sel_∞(f,K,S)[γ−1] with finite index; hence (2.7.1) #X_𝔭(f,K,S) = ∞ ⟺ #(X_∞(f,K,S)/(γ−1)X_∞(f,K,S)) = ∞. If L^S_𝔭(f,1) = 0 then L^S_𝔭(f) ∈ (γ−1), so under Proposition 2.7.2 Ch_Λ(f,K,S) ⊆ (γ−1) and the coinvariants are infinite, giving (2.7.2) L^S_𝔭(f,1) = 0 ⟹ #X_𝔭(f,K,S) = ∞. Finally, since H^1(K_𝔭,V) ↪ H^1(I_𝔭,V), one has H^1_𝔭(K,V) = ker{H^1(G_{K,S},V) → H^1(I_𝔭,V)} and its image in H^1(G_{K,S},W) is the maximal divisible subgroup of Sel_𝔭(f,K,S).
items.locator: §2.7, the paragraphs containing (2.7.1) and (2.7.2), Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Proposition 2.7.3: a vanishing p-adic L-value forces a 𝔭-relaxed Selmer class
items.statement: Proposition 2.7.3. If the hypotheses of Proposition 2.7.2 hold, then L^S_𝔭(f,1) = 0 implies H^1_𝔭(K,V) ≠ 0.
items.locator: Proposition 2.7.3, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Lemma 2.8.1: (irr) and (res) imply (irr_K)
items.statement: Lemma 2.8.1. If (irr) and (res) hold, then so does (irr_K). (Proof: let ℓ | N be a prime at which ρ̄_{f,λ} is ramified; as ℓ || N the action of I_ℓ on V is unipotent and factors through tame inertia, so for a topological generator τ_ℓ of tame inertia at ℓ the element ρ_{f,λ}(τ_ℓ), hence ρ̄_{f,λ}(τ_ℓ), is unipotent of order a power of p; since τ_ℓ² ∈ G_K, the image of ρ̄_{f,λ}|_{G_K} contains a non-trivial unipotent element. If ρ̄_{f,λ}|_{G_K} were reducible over k̄ its image would lie in a torus, split or non-split, or in a Borel of GL_2(k); the torus is excluded by the unipotent element, so the image lies in a Borel, and since the image of G_K is normalised by the image of G_Q the image of G_Q lies in the same Borel, contradicting (irr).)
items.locator: Lemma 2.8.1 with its proof, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354; the printed proof writes 'ρ̄_{f,λ} is reducible' where the hypothesis for contradiction must be on ρ̄_{f,λ}|_{G_K} (source issue E3)

items.name: The proof of Theorem B
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem B, (sqf), (odd) and (big) hold by assumption; (a) gives (flt) and (ord); (b) is (irr) and (res), so (irr_K) holds by Lemma 2.8.1; (c) is (spl); (e) gives (sgn) by Lemma 2.2.1. Propositions 2.7.2 and 2.7.3 then give: H^1_𝔭(K,V) = 0 implies L^S_𝔭(f,1) ≠ 0. Hypothesis (e) gives H^1_𝔭(K,V) = 0 by Lemma 2.3.2, and (d) is (ram), so Corollary 2.6.2 gives P_K(f) ≠ 0. The rank of A_f(K) is [M_f:Q] times the M_{f,p}-rank of A_f(K) ⊗ Q_p, at most dim_L H^1_f(K,V) = 1 by (e), and is non-zero since P_K(f) ≠ 0; hence rank_Z A_f(K) = [M_f:Q], and by Proposition 2.5.1 and Corollary 2.5.2, ord_{s=1}L(f,K,s) = 1 and ord_{s=1}L(A_f/K,s) = [M_f:Q]. Finiteness of Ш(A_f/K) reduces to that of Ш(A_f) and Ш(A_f^D); since L(f,K,s) = L(f,s)L(f ⊗ χ_D,s) has order 1 at s = 1, one factor has order 1 and the other order 0, and Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin applies.

items.name: Remark 2.9.1: where each hypothesis is used
items.statement: Remark 2.9.1 records, in thirteen items, the provenance of each hypothesis: (i) squarefreeness comes from Wan and Brooks, and squarefreeness at the primes dividing (D,N) from Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna; (ii) p ≥ 5 is imposed for convenience in Wan; (iii) D odd is imposed in Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna, Brooks and Wan, and stems from gaps in the theta correspondence in residue characteristic 2; (iv) p ∤ N is used in the p-adic Gross–Zagier formulas and to simplify the appeal to the parity theorem; (v) ordinarity is used only for Wan's theorem and for the parity theorem, and a finite non-critical slope version of Proposition 2.7.2 together with the corresponding parity result would suffice; (vi) irreducibility and (res) are required in Wan, the latter to produce a transfer of π to a definite U(2) ramified at ℓ; (vii) the splitting of p in K is needed for all three p-adic inputs and for Lemma 2.3.2, and is the hardest to relax; (viii) the hypotheses in (d) are needed to appeal to Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna, which requires ε_ℓ(f,K) = +1 for ℓ | (N,D); (ix) one-dimensionality of H^1_f(K,V) is used to know beforehand that ε(f,K) = −1; (x) the injectivity at p is needed for H^1_𝔭(K,V) = 0, and Wei Zhang obtains a version of Theorem B without it at the expense of Tamagawa hypotheses; (xi) the local hypotheses can likely be relaxed, for instance using Liu–Zhang–Zhang's general form of Proposition 2.6.1; (xii) the CM analogue is Rubin's Theorems 8.1, 8.2 and can also be proved along the present lines using the CM main conjecture and Rubin Theorem 9.5 or BDP Theorem 2; (xiii) the method can give an alternative proof of the base case of Wei Zhang's induction that avoids Skinner–Urban and should work at supersingular primes.
items.locator: Remark 2.9.1, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Comparison with Wei Zhang's theorem on Kolyvagin's conjecture
items.statement: Wei Zhang proves many cases of a conjecture of Kolyvagin, showing that the p-adic Selmer group of A_f is often spanned by classes derived from Heegner points, and obtains a theorem similar to Theorem B. That theorem does not require the injectivity of the restriction map at the primes above p — the second half of hypothesis (e) — but crucially requires that the Tamagawa factors at the primes that split in K or are congruent to ±1 modulo p be indivisible by p, whereas Theorem B imposes no hypothesis on Tamagawa factors. There is substantial overlap but neither result subsumes the other; Zhang's proof also rests on Iwasawa theory, in his case on Skinner–Urban.
items.locator: §1, the paragraph before the acknowledgements, and Remark 2.9.1(x), Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (W. Zhang, Selmer groups and the indivisibility of Heegner points, Camb. J. Math. 2 (2014))

items.name: Density one of the ordinary primes for a non-CM newform
items.statement: For a newform f of weight two that is not a CM form, the set of primes p ∤ N such that f is ordinary with respect to some λ | p has density 1. (If f is not ordinary at any λ | p for a p ∤ N greater than 4 and unramified in M_f, then the norm of a_p(f), of absolute value at most (2p^{1/2})^{[M_f:Q]} by the Ramanujan bound, is an integer divisible by p^{[M_f:Q]}, so a_p(f) = 0; and the set of primes with a_p(f) = 0 has density zero.)
items.locator: §3, first paragraph, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Serre, Quelques applications du théorème de densité de Chebotarev, §7.2, Corollary 2)

items.name: Irreducibility of the residual representation for large p
items.statement: For a newform f without complex multiplication, ρ̄_{f,λ} is irreducible for all λ | p once p is sufficiently large.
items.locator: §3, second paragraph, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Ribet, On ℓ-adic representations attached to modular forms II, Glasgow Math. J. 27 (1985), Theorem 2.1)

items.name: Ramification of the residual representation at every prime dividing N
items.statement: For p sufficiently large, ρ̄_{f,λ} is ramified at all primes dividing N. (If for some ℓ | N there were arbitrarily large p and λ | p with ρ̄_{f,λ} unramified at ℓ, then by the finiteness of the set of newforms of weight 2 and level dividing N and by Ribet's level-lowering theorem there would be a newform g of weight 2 and level prime to ℓ congruent to f modulo primes of arbitrarily large characteristic; their prime-to-Np coefficients would then be equal, so f = g by multiplicity one, a contradiction.)
items.locator: §3, second paragraph, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Ribet, On modular representations of Gal(Q̄/Q) arising from modular forms, Invent. Math. 100 (1990))

items.name: The choice of the auxiliary imaginary quadratic field
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem A one chooses an imaginary quadratic K of discriminant D with: (i) 2 and p split in K, so D is odd and hypothesis (c) of Theorem B holds; (ii) if for some odd ℓ the representation π_ℓ is the twist of the special representation by the unramified quadratic character, then K is ramified at ℓ and all other prime divisors of N split in K; (iii) if there is no such π_ℓ but there are two odd primes ℓ_1, ℓ_2 with π_{ℓ_1}, π_{ℓ_2} special, then ℓ_1 and ℓ_2 are inert in K and all other prime divisors of N split in K; (iv) L(f ⊗ χ_D,1) ≠ 0. Conditions (i)–(ii) give ε(f,K) = −ε_ℓ(π,K) = −1 and (i)–(iii) give ε(f,K) = −ε_{ℓ_1}(π,K)ε_{ℓ_2}(π,K) = −1, so ε(f ⊗ χ_D) = −ε(f) = +1 and (iv) can then also be arranged; (i)–(iii) imply hypotheses (b), (c), (d) of Theorem B.
items.locator: §3, the list (i)–(iv) and the paragraph following it, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: Non-vanishing of quadratic twists in the sign +1 branch
items.statement: Given a newform f and finitely many local conditions on the discriminant compatible with a sign ε(f ⊗ χ_D) = +1, there is an imaginary quadratic field K of discriminant D satisfying those conditions with L(f ⊗ χ_D,1) ≠ 0. This is Theorem B of Friedberg–Hoffstein.
items.locator: Used in §3, condition (iv), Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Friedberg–Hoffstein, Ann. of Math. (2) 142 (1995), 385–423, Theorem B)
items.note: BSD.2 plans exactly the quadratic-twist non-vanishing theorem with finitely many prescribed splitting and local conditions compatible with the functional equation, naming the BFH/Friedberg–Hoffstein unfolding as its proof route.

items.name: The proof of Theorem A
items.statement: Fix p ≥ 5, p ∤ N and λ | p with f ordinary at λ and ρ̄_{f,λ} irreducible and ramified at every prime dividing N. The hypotheses rank_Z A_f(Q) = [M_f:Q] and Ш(A_f)[p^∞] finite give dim_L H^1_f(Q,V) = 1 by the analogue of Lemma 2.2.2 over Q, whence ε(f) = −1 by the parity theorem. Choose K as above; the non-vanishing L(f ⊗ χ_D,1) ≠ 0 makes A_f^D(Q) and Ш(A_f^D) finite by Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin, or alternatively by Kato, so rank_Z A_f(K) = [M_f:Q] and Ш(A_f/K)[p^∞] is finite, and hypothesis (e) of Theorem B holds by Lemma 2.2.2. Theorem B gives ord_{s=1}L(f,K,s) = 1, and since L(f,K,s) = L(f,s)L(f ⊗ χ_D,s) with L(f ⊗ χ_D,1) ≠ 0, ord_{s=1}L(f,s) = 1.

items.name: Kato's Euler system as an alternative to Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin at rank zero
items.statement: The finiteness of A_f^D(Q) and Ш(A_f^D) from L(f ⊗ χ_D,1) ≠ 0 can be deduced from Kato's Euler system instead of from the work of Gross, Zagier and Kolyvagin.
items.locator: §3, the paragraph deducing hypothesis (e), Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354 (Kato, Astérisque 295 (2004), 117–290)
items.note: KatoEulerSystems L4 plans the non-vanishing and cohomological theorems of Kato's system and BSD.4 records the Kato route to the analytic-rank-zero statement as an explicitly scoped alternative.

items.name: The deduction of Theorem C from Theorem B
items.statement: Hypothesis (c) of Theorem C implies that H^1_f(Q,V) → H^1_f(Q_p,V) ≅ Q_p is an isomorphism. The representation E[p] must be ramified at some odd prime ℓ of bad reduction for E, again by Ribet's level-lowering results. An appropriate imaginary quadratic field K that is inert or ramified at ℓ is then chosen, according to whether E has split or non-split reduction at ℓ, and Theorem B applies.
items.locator: §3, final paragraph, Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354

items.name: The proof of Theorem E
items.statement: The argument is that of Theorem A with two changes: the hypotheses now imply ε(f) = +1, and K is chosen to satisfy (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)' ord_{s=1}L(f ⊗ χ_D,s) = 1, which is possible because ε(f ⊗ χ_D) will equal −1. Theorem B then gives ord_{s=1}L(f,K,s) = 1, which by the choice of K forces L(f,1) ≠ 0.

prerequisites.citation: Xin Wan, "Iwasawa main conjecture for Rankin–Selberg p-adic L-functions", Algebra & Number Theory 14 (2020), no. 2, 383–483
prerequisites.why: Theorem 1.2 is the only source of the divisibility Ch_Λ(f,K,S) ⊆ (L^S_𝔭(f)) that makes Proposition 2.7.2 and hence the whole argument work. Its proof is the U(3,1) Eisenstein-congruence method of Skinner–Urban, with the two-variable p-adic L-function 𝓛^{Σ,Hida}_{f_0,K,ξ} over Γ_K ≅ Z_p²; its hypotheses are exactly (big), (ord), (spl), (res), (irr_K) and the squarefreeness of N. Nothing in this paper reproves it. The 2013 Columbia preprint cited in the arXiv version and the published paper are not interchangeable.

prerequisites.citation: Massimo Bertolini, Henri Darmon and Kartik Prasanna, "p-adic Rankin L-series and rational points on CM elliptic curves", Pacific J. Math. 260 (2012), no. 2, 261–303, and "Generalized Heegner cycles and p-adic Rankin L-series", Duke Math. J. 162 (2013), no. 6, 1033–1148
prerequisites.why: Theorem 3.12 of the first is Proposition 2.6.1 in Case I, and the second constructs the anticyclotomic p-adic L-function L_p(f,χ) on Σ^{(2)}_{cc}(𝔫) with the interpolation formula whose imprimitive variant is L^S_𝔭(f). Their hypotheses — N squarefree at the primes dividing (D,N), D odd, p ∤ N split in K, ε_ℓ(f,K) = +1 for ℓ | (N,D) — are carried into Theorem B as (d), (odd) and (flt).

prerequisites.citation: Ernest Hunter Brooks, "Shimura curves and special values of p-adic L-functions", Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN 2015, no. 12, 4177–4241
prerequisites.why: Proposition 8.13 is Proposition 2.6.1 in Case II, on the Shimura curve of discriminant N^- with an Eichler order of level N^+, together with the normalisation of the Jacquet–Langlands transfer f_B over M_f (§2.8) and the constant α(f,f_{GL_2})^{-1} that is C(f,K) here.

prerequisites.citation: Xinyi Yuan, Shou-Wu Zhang and Wei Zhang, "The Gross–Zagier Formula on Shimura Curves", Annals of Mathematics Studies 184, Princeton University Press, 2013
prerequisites.why: Theorem 3.13 is the height identity behind Proposition 2.5.1, and §§1.2.2, 3.1.3 and 3.2.5 supply the normalised Hodge divisor ξ, the point P(f_1) and the pairing f_1 ∘ f_2^∨ used in the computation. The whole reduction of Theorem B to the non-vanishing of P_K(f) rests on it.

Theorem 12.2.3, the parity theorem for Selmer groups of modular forms ordinary at λ, is used twice: to deduce ε(f,K) = −1 in Lemma 2.2.1 and ε(f) = −1 in §3. It is the only reason the sign hypothesis (sgn), required by all three of Yuan–Zhang–Zhang, Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna and Wan, can be verified from the arithmetic hypotheses of Theorem A.

prerequisites.citation: Ralph Greenberg, "Iwasawa theory and p-adic deformations of motives", Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 55, Part 2, Amer. Math. Soc. (1994), 193–223
prerequisites.why: §3's Panchishkin condition and §4's Selmer groups for a deformation, together with Conjecture 4.1, are the framework in which Sel_∞(f,K,S), its characteristic ideal and Conjecture 2.7.1 are formulated; §2.7 is an explicit generalisation of that setting to G_K-representations.

prerequisites.citation: Solomon Friedberg and Jeffrey Hoffstein, "Nonvanishing theorems for automorphic L-functions on GL(2)", Ann. of Math. (2) 142 (1995), no. 2, 385–423
prerequisites.why: Theorem B supplies the imaginary quadratic field K with L(f ⊗ χ_D,1) ≠ 0 and the prescribed local behaviour at 2, p and the primes dividing N; without it the choice of K in §3 and §4 cannot be made.

prerequisites.citation: Kenneth A. Ribet, "On ℓ-adic representations attached to modular forms II", Glasgow Math. J. 27 (1985), 185–194, and "On modular representations of Gal(Q̄/Q) arising from modular forms", Invent. Math. 100 (1990), no. 2, 431–476
prerequisites.why: The first gives the irreducibility of ρ̄_{f,λ} for large p and the second the level-lowering theorem from which §3 deduces that ρ̄_{f,λ} is ramified at every prime dividing N for large p; hypothesis (b) of Theorem B is verified from them.

prerequisites.citation: Jean-Pierre Serre, "Quelques applications du théorème de densité de Chebotarev", Inst. Hautes Études Sci. Publ. Math. 54 (1981), 323–401
prerequisites.why: §7.2, Corollary 2, the density zero of the set of primes with a_p(f) = 0 for a non-CM form, is what makes the set of admissible ordinary primes in §3 have density one.

prerequisites.citation: Manya Brakočević, "Anticyclotomic p-adic L-function of central critical Rankin–Selberg L-value", Int. Math. Res. Not. IMRN 2011, no. 21, 4967–5018, with Ellen Eischen, Michael Harris, Jian-Shu Li and Christopher Skinner, "p-adic L-functions for unitary groups", arXiv:1602.01776
prerequisites.why: These are what upgrade the continuous function on Γ constructed by Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna and Brooks to an element of the Iwasawa algebra O^ur[[Γ]], by extending the interpolation to characters ramified above p. Without that the Iwasawa-theoretic argument of §2.7 cannot be stated.

prerequisites.citation: Wei Zhang, "Selmer groups and the indivisibility of Heegner points", Camb. J. Math. 2 (2014), no. 2, 191–253
prerequisites.why: The closest comparable theorem, obtained from Kolyvagin's conjecture instead: it drops the injectivity at p but requires Tamagawa factors indivisible by p. The report and the item zhang-comparison record that neither result subsumes the other; a blueprint should plan both statements separately.

prerequisites.citation: Manjul Bhargava and Christopher Skinner, "A positive proportion of elliptic curves over Q have rank one", J. Ramanujan Math. Soc. 29 (2014), no. 2, 221–242
prerequisites.why: Theorem D of this paper. It is the main consumer of Theorem B, through variations of the kind exemplified by Theorem C, and its Selmer-distribution input belongs to ArithmeticStatistics rather than here.

prerequisites.citation: Karl Rubin, "p-adic L-functions and rational points on elliptic curves with complex multiplication", Invent. Math. 107 (1992), no. 2, 323–350
prerequisites.why: Theorems 8.1 and 8.2 are the CM analogue of Theorem A, proved by a different route (Rubin's main conjecture, Perrin-Riou's p-adic Gross–Zagier formula, Bertrand's non-degeneracy); Theorem 9.5 is the CM analogue of Proposition 2.6.1, by which Remark 2.9.1(xii) says the present method also covers the CM case. The cases covered here are disjoint from Rubin's.

routes.title: Rank-zero and rank-one Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer theory, Part II: the p-converse to Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin
routes.brief:
This coalesces with the RankOneConverse Part II of RankZeroOneBSD that the maintainer routed for this very paper (DESIGN-SKINNER, issue #951, area iwasawa) and that PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22 already extended with the Eisenstein-prime branch; it keeps that job's final theorems and adds the source items of Skinner, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329-354, itself.

Final theorems. (A) For a newform f in S_2(Gamma_0(N)) of trivial nebentypus with N squarefree, if either some odd prime l has pi_l the twist of the special representation by the unramified quadratic character, or two odd primes l_1, l_2 have pi_{l_i} special, then rank_Z A_f(Q) = [M_f:Q] together with #Sha(A_f) finite implies ord_{s=1}L(f,s) = 1; equivalently (A') for a semistable elliptic curve with non-split multiplicative reduction at one odd prime or split multiplicative reduction at two. (B) The p-adic criterion over an imaginary quadratic field K of odd discriminant with hypotheses (a)-(e), whose conclusion is ord_{s=1}L(f,K,s) = 1, rank_Z A_f(K) = [M_f:Q] = ord_{s=1}L(A_f/K,s) and Sha(A_f/K) finite. (C) The mod-p Selmer criterion Sel_p(E) = Z/pZ plus the local condition at p. (E) The analogous rank-zero statement, an alternative proof of a special case of Skinner-Urban and Wan. Theorem D of the paper, the positive proportion of curves of rank one, is a consumer owned by ArithmeticStatistics.

Import, never re-plan: RankZeroOneBSD BSD.0-BSD.4 for analytic L-functions, twists, quadratic descent, the Friedberg-Hoffstein non-vanishing and the forward Gross-Zagier-Kolyvagin direction; HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.0-HE.1 and HE.7 for ring class fields, CM points and the classical descent; GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.0, GZ.3, GZ.8 for the normalisations and the Yuan-Zhang-Zhang height identity, and GZ.9 for the BDP/Brooks p-adic L-function and the p-adic Waldspurger formula; AutomorphicCongruences L2 for Wan's two-variable U(3,1) divisibility; ModularIwasawaMainConjectures L0 for the Greenberg/Panchishkin formulation and L1, L5 for the rank-zero converse; SelmerIwasawaCohomology L1-L4 for Bloch-Kato and Greenberg Selmer groups, duality and control; PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4-L5 for characteristic ideals; AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.1, R19.4, R19.5 for the representation V; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0 for algebraic Hecke characters and their p-adic avatars; KatoEulerSystems L4 for the alternative rank-zero input.

Construct here: the two cases I and II for the pair (f,K) and the Heegner point P_K(f) in A_f(K) tensor M_f with its epsilon_f-normalisation and the comparison of the cusp, Hodge and epsilon_f normalisations; the hypotheses (sqf), (sgn), (ram), (flt), (odd), (L-lrg), (big), (ord), (spl), (res), (irr), (irr_K) and the implications among them, in particular Lemma 2.8.1; the strict and p-relaxed Selmer groups with Lemmas 2.3.1 and 2.3.2, which is where the splitting of p in K is used; the big Galois module M = T tensor Lambda^*(Psi^{-1}), its Selmer group, characteristic ideal and Conjecture 2.7.1, stated over Lambda^ur tensor_O L as in the published version; Proposition 2.7.2 and its deduction from Wan's theorem by specialising the two-variable objects along gamma to psi_0(gamma)^{-1}gamma; the control diagram giving (2.7.1) and (2.7.2) and hence Proposition 2.7.3; and the assembly of Theorem B, the choice of the auxiliary K in section 3 and the deductions of Theorems A, C and E.

Keep the published hypotheses and coefficient rings: the arXiv preprint of 2014 places the anticyclotomic p-adic L-function in O[[Gamma]] and states Conjecture 2.7.1 and Proposition 2.7.2 in Lambda tensor Q_p, which the published version corrects (source issue E1). Wei Zhang's theorem on Kolyvagin's conjecture gives a comparable but incomparable statement, dropping the injectivity at p and adding Tamagawa hypotheses; the two should be stated separately and neither presented as subsuming the other.
routes.reason: The maintainer routed this paper to the Part II RankOneConverse of RankZeroOneBSD (DESIGN-SKINNER), and PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22 already reused that candidate for the Eisenstein-prime branch of the same p-converse; the review of PAPER-BURUNGALE-TIAN-26 asked for a single owner of the p-converse property. This route therefore reuses the same id, title and area rather than proposing anything new. The parent proves the Gross–Zagier–Kolyvagin direction at BSD.3 and BSD.4 and has no layer for the converse, and BSD.5–BSD.9 plan leading-term formulas, not a Selmer-to-analytic implication.

L4 plans the arithmetic examples and conjectures attached to Selmer groups, including the Bloch–Kato and ordinary local conditions and the statement of the Coates–Perrin-Riou/Panchishkin conjecture, but no parity theorem, and nothing else in the atlas plans one: RankZeroOneBSD BSD.0 plans only the root-number parity of the analytic order. This source adds Nekovář's parity theorem for the Selmer groups of a modular form ordinary at λ (Selmer complexes, Theorem 12.2.3), which is what forces ε(f) = −1 from a one-dimensional Selmer group in §3 and, through Lemma 2.2.1, ε(f,K) = −1 from an odd-dimensional one. It is an input quoted, not proved, in this paper, and it is the hypothesis (sgn) on which the Gross–Zagier and p-adic Gross–Zagier formulas both depend.

R19.1 constructs the weight-two representation attached to a newform with its coefficient field and lattices and R19.3 the compatible system and its purity. This source adds the three statements about the family {ρ̄_{f,λ}} that §3 needs and that no layer plans: that for a newform without complex multiplication the set of primes p with f ordinary at some λ | p has density one, which combines the Ramanujan bound with Serre's Chebotarev theorem that {p : a_p(f) = 0} has density zero; that ρ̄_{f,λ} is irreducible for all λ | p once p is large (Ribet); and that for large p it is ramified at every prime dividing N, which is deduced from Ribet's level-lowering theorem (planned at SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.2) together with the finiteness of the set of newforms of weight two and level dividing N and multiplicity one. These are statements about the compatible system as a whole, not about one member of it.

GZ.9 plans the BDP/Brooks p-adic L-function with its interpolation range, CM periods and removed Euler factors, and the p-adic Waldspurger identity at the weight-two point. This source adds the two facts about that function that Skinner's argument needs and that GZ.9 does not state. First, integrality: the functions of Bertolini–Darmon–Prasanna and of Brooks are a priori only continuous on Γ, and membership in the Iwasawa algebra O^ur[[Γ]] — without which the Iwasawa-theoretic argument of §2.7 cannot even be formulated — requires extending the interpolation formulas to characters ramified above p, as in Brakočević, or the constructions of Eischen–Harris–Li–Skinner and Wan. Second, the precise dictionary between the imprimitive L^S_𝔭(f) used here and the published L_p(f,χ): the character sets Σ^{(2)}_{cc}(𝔫) and Σ^{(2)}_{cc}(𝔫^+), the removal of the Euler factors at the primes of S not dividing p, and the identities relating C(f,χ,1), w(f,χ) and α(f,f_{GL_2})^{-1} to the constants used here. Both are comparison statements about the object GZ.9 owns.

sourceIssues.printed: "There is an anticyclotomic p-adic L-function L^S_𝔭(f) ∈ O[[Γ]] such that for ψ ∈ Σ^c_𝔭 …"; "Let Λ = O[[Γ]]"; Conjecture 2.7.1: "Ch_Λ(f,K,S) = (L^S_𝔭(f)) in Λ ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p"; Proposition 2.7.2: "Under the above assumptions, Ch_Λ(f,K,S) ⊆ (L^S_𝔭(f)) in Λ ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p"
sourceIssues.correction: The published version reads: O^ur is the ring of integers of the completion of the maximal unramified extension L^ur of L; L^S_𝔭(f) ∈ O^ur[[Γ]] and the unit W of w(f,ψ) = ψ(W) lies in O^ur[[Γ]]^×; Λ = O[[Γ]] and Λ^ur = O^ur[[Γ]]; Conjecture 2.7.1 reads "Ch_Λ(f,K,S) and L^S_𝔭(f) generate the same ideal of Λ^ur ⊗_O L" and is called essentially the Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjecture; Proposition 2.7.2 reads "the ideal of Λ^ur ⊗_O L generated by Ch_Λ(f,K,S) is contained in the ideal generated by L^S_𝔭(f)".
sourceIssues.reason: The interpolation formula defining L^S_𝔭(f) has the p-adic period Ω_p^{4n} of a CM elliptic curve E_0 in it, and Ω_p is a unit of the completion of the maximal unramified extension, not of O; the same is true of the two-variable function 𝓛^{Σ,Hida}_{f_0,K,ξ} ∈ O^ur[[Γ_K]] of Wan's theorem, to which the deduction of Proposition 2.7.2 specialises. So the element L^S_𝔭(f) of the preprint's Conjecture 2.7.1 and Proposition 2.7.2 need not lie in O[[Γ]] and those two statements are not the ones the sources prove. The published version's own deduction makes this explicit: it specialises Wan's inclusion of ideals of O^ur[[Γ_K]] ⊗_O L along O^ur[[Γ_K]] → Λ^ur and concludes about ideals of Λ^ur ⊗_O L. Everything else in the preprint and the published version agrees: the 19 numbered statements carry the same numbers and, apart from these coefficient rings, the same text.
sourceIssues.known: Corrected in the published version, Ann. of Math. (2) 191 (2020), 329–354, §§2.6–2.7 (pp. 342–346), which introduces O^ur and Λ^ur and restates Conjecture 2.7.1 and Proposition 2.7.2 over Λ^ur ⊗_O L. The items of this extraction use the published form.

sourceIssues.printed: The corresponding inclusion of the ideal of Λ^ur ⊗_O L generated by Ch_Λ(f,K,S) into the ideal generated by L^S_𝔭(f) then follows easily, using that the rings O^ur[[Γ_K]] and Λ^ur are unique factorization ideals and the various characteristic ideals are principal (cf. sourceIssues.correction: "unique factorization ideals" should read "unique factorization domains"
sourceIssues.reason: The property being used is that the two completed group rings are UFDs, so that an inclusion of principal ideals can be tested factor by factor after specialisation; "unique factorization ideal" is not a notion, and the reference given, Corollary 3.8 of Skinner–Urban, is the statement that these Iwasawa algebras are unique factorization domains with principal characteristic ideals. The sentence was read directly from the content stream of the published PDF, where it is unchanged from the preprint.

sourceIssues.locator: §2.8, the proof of Lemma 2.8.1, the sentence beginning "Suppose now that", published p. 347; the same sentence is in arXiv:1405.7294v1
sourceIssues.printed: Let k be the residue field of L. Suppose now that ρ̄_{f,λ} is reducible over k̄. Then the image of ρ̄_{f,λ}|_{G_K} is contained in either a torus (split or non-split) or a Borel of GL_2(k).
sourceIssues.correction: the hypothesis for contradiction must be that ρ̄_{f,λ}|_{G_K} is reducible over k̄, not that ρ̄_{f,λ} is
sourceIssues.reason: Lemma 2.8.1 asserts that (irr) and (res) imply (irr_K), so the argument must assume the failure of (irr_K) — the reducibility of the restriction to G_K — and derive a contradiction with (irr). As printed, the sentence assumes the failure of (irr) and then, four lines later, concludes "contradicting (irr)", which proves nothing. That the intended hypothesis is on the restriction is confirmed by the next sentence, which speaks only of the image of ρ̄_{f,λ}|_{G_K}, and by the dichotomy offered there: a reducible two-dimensional representation of G_K whose restriction is semisimple has image in a torus and otherwise in a Borel, which is exactly the case division the proof then makes.
